# `del_obj`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Delete a named object from a named object list.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / probable (64-bit build; 32-bit build probable) |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0xe82a0, ObjListConfig::DelObj @0x6c3c30 (64-bit build) |

Resolves the list and the object by display name and removes the object's subtree from the persistent object-list configuration.

Side effects: Removes an object entry from the persistent XML configuration, synchronously. No event is emitted by the handler.

## Request params

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"del_obj"`. [READ] |
| `params` | object\|array | no | - | Object with list and obj, or a positional array of two strings [list, obj]. Any other container yields an empty map and therefore 105. No defaults and no further validation. [READ] |

| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (both) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 105 | list or obj missing, null or not a string (or wrong params container) | `expected string param` |
| 236 | The configuration root, the list or the object is not found | `xml item is not found` |
| 234 | Lower RemoveChild step: configuration file name storage is empty | `xml file name is empty` |
| 229 | Lower RemoveChild step: the XML key could not be opened | `fail to open xml key` |
| 230 | Lower RemoveChild step: the XML item could not be deleted | `fail to delete xml item` |
| 200 | Dispatcher: request has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: method missing or not a string | `invalid request` |

Lower-level codes are established for the 64-bit RemoveChild only; 32-bit equivalence is not asserted. Other lower failures are unresolved.

## Example

Request, delete:

```json
{"id":51,"method":"del_obj","params":{"list":"Winter targets","obj":"Example nebula"}}
```

Request, delete-array-form:

```json
{"id":52,"method":"del_obj","params":["Winter targets","Example nebula"]}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"del_obj","result":0,"code":0,"id":51}
```
